arbaeen_ahadith.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear” (Arbaʿīn 6)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which tribe of the Anṣār was al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA from?

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA was born {{c1::14 months after the Hijrah}} — {{c2::the first child born to the Anṣār}} after it — to parents who were {{c3::both Companions}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How old was al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA when the Prophet ﷺ died?
For what two qualities was al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA known?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Great generosity, and skill in poetry

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How and when did al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA die?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: He was killed, in 64 or 65 AH

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How many aḥādīth did al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr RA narrate?
What do some scholars say about reflecting on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Whoever reflects on it will come to see all the acts of Islam, inward and outward

arbaeen_ahadith.text: The ḥadīth “the lawful is clear” divides actions into three: {{c1::the clearly lawful — what the Sharīʿah has explicitly permitted}}; {{c2::the clearly unlawful — what it has explicitly forbidden}}; and {{c3::the doubtful — what lies between, which many people don't know}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why are some matters “doubtful”, according to the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Not because the Sharīʿah is unclear, but because the person doesn't know — they are doubtful relative to the individual's knowledge

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does the Prophet ﷺ advise about doubtful matters, and why?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Avoiding them is much safer: it protects one's religion and honour — <bdi>فَقَدِ اسْتَبْرَأَ لِدِينِهِ وَعِرْضِهِ</bdi>

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is the standing of someone who engages in doubtful matters?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: He isn't violating the Sharīʿah, or counted as disobedient — but whoever keeps doing doubtful things will in the end fall into the unlawful

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What role do disliked acts play, according to the lesson on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: They are a checkpoint between a person and the unlawful. Whoever indulges in them often falls into the unlawful, and grows careless.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What did Abū al-Dardāʾ RA call complete taqwā?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Leaving something one believes permissible, for fear it may be unlawful — good to practise on ourselves, but not a standard we hold others to

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What did Ibn ʿUmar RA call leaving doubtful matters?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A veil between himself and the unlawful

arbaeen_ahadith.front: To whom does the Prophet ﷺ compare someone who keeps engaging in doubtful matters, in the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A shepherd who keeps grazing his flock along someone else's land — the <bdi>حِمَى</bdi>, a private pasture — until some of the animals stray over the line

arbaeen_ahadith.text: “Truly, every king has {{c1::a sanctuary}}, and Allah's sanctuary is {{c2::what He has made unlawful}}”
arbaeen_ahadith.extra: <bdi>أَلَا وَإِنَّ لِكُلِّ مَلِكٍ حِمًى، أَلَا وَإِنَّ حِمَى اللهِ مَحَارِمُهُ</bdi> (Arbaʿīn 6)
arbaeen_ahadith.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 6 — the text in translation

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does the Prophet ﷺ say of the heart at the end of the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: In the body is a morsel of flesh (<bdi>مُضْغَة</bdi>): when it is sound, the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — truly, it is the heart

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How does the lesson on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear” relate the spiritual heart to the physical one?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The spiritual heart is connected to the physical heart, just as the soul is somehow connected to the body

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Where does tazkiyah come in, according to the lesson on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: In purifying the heart: removing its blameworthy qualities and replacing them with praiseworthy ones

vocab.source: Arbaʿīn, Ḥadīth 6 — vocab in the class notes, 2026-10-21

quduri.front: Which materials does Abū Yūsuf allow for tayammum, against Abū Ḥanīfah and Muḥammad?
quduri.back: Only soil and sand. They allow any pure substance of the earth that doesn't burn to ash and isn't a metal.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-21

quduri.back: Everything that nullifies wuḍūʾ — and gaining access to water, or the ability to use it
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-21

quduri.front: What becomes of a prayer already completed with tayammum, once water becomes available?
quduri.back: It stands — it need not be repeated
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-21

quduri.front: What is recommended for someone without water who reasonably hopes to find it before the prayer's time ends?
quduri.back: To delay the prayer toward the end of its time: if water comes, make wuḍūʾ; if not, make tayammum and pray
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-21

quduri.front: A traveller forgets he has water, makes tayammum and prays. How do the Ḥanafī imams rule?
quduri.back: Abū Ḥanīfah and Muḥammad: he needn't repeat the prayer. Abū Yūsuf: he must.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-21

quduri.meaning: preponderant belief — near certainty; in tayammum, the standard for concluding there is no water
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-21

qud-269.back: Any pure substance of the earth that does not burn to ash and is not a metal — soil, sand, stone, but not plants or wood. This is Abū Ḥanīfah's and Muḥammad's view.
